transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2025-04-07
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Liam O'Connor, Maya Singh (Redwood); Oscar Reid, Priya Narang, Daniel Cho (Bluewing Freight)

Summary:
00:00 - Quick status and renewal intent (Bluewing signals intent to renew but wants capacity bump + APAC sovereign pilot).
00:35 - Deep dive on traffic patterns, latency targets, and security controls.
01:20 - Agreement on next steps: pricing, traffic profile, pilot plan, security deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — appreciate it. Quick check, is this still a good time for you all?
[00:05] Oscar (Bluewing): Yeah, yeah, all good. Sorry, just coming out of another sync, so you'll hear a little rustle.
[00:12] Priya (Bluewing): We're good. We've got Daniel on for the sec bits.
[00:15] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi team, Maya here, I'll handle the throughput/latency bits and set up the perf runs we chatted about.
[00:20] Liam: Great. High level, Oscar was clear earlier — Bluewing wants to renew but needs a committed uplift and an APAC proof we can run in private for sovereignty. Wanted to go through numbers and the SLOs today.

[01:02] Oscar: Yep, correct. We're seeing a seasonal 3x spike during end-of-quarter shipping windows, and our current headroom is getting tight. Latency is the other thing — customers complain when routing decisions are slow in APAC.
[01:18] Maya: Can you share what you mean by "routing decisions" latency — is that the model inference p95 or the whole round trip, DB lookups included?
[01:25] Priya: Mostly inference p95. We do a quick ensemble: a classification call plus a short embed for rerank. So two model calls back-to-back, usually under 600 tokens each, but when both fire it gets chewy.
[01:40] Liam: That's helpful. So short-ish sequences but bursty. For capacity we'd usually recommend pinned dedicated instances for the sustained qps and a burst pool to absorb spikes — that keeps unit costs predictable.

[02:12] Daniel (sec): On the sovereignty side, we need the private control plane option. Can't have metadata leaving the APAC VPC in plaintext, and KMS integration is non-negotiable. Also audit logs retention for 2 years.
[02:30] Liam: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integrations; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. We'll flag that for the security deep-dive.

[03:05] Oscar: Before we get into pricing, we need to be clear on failover. If APAC capacity is saturated, what's the fallback? We can't have routing send traffic to US with five-second penalties.
[03:20] Maya: We typically route by policy. For low-latency SLOs you can pin region-only routing; there are also options to fall back to a compatible quantized model variant in-region. That degrades quality a little but keeps latency under the SLO.
[03:40] Priya: Ok, interesting. We would prefer graceful degradation over cross-region hop.

[04:10] Liam: So proposal: 12-month renewal, committed capacity in APAC sized at 1.5x your current sustained qps (we sketched initial numbers from usage you shared in Jan), plus a shared burst bucket for the 3x seasonal spikes. Include an option to start a private APAC pilot for 90 days — private control plane, KMS, audit export.
[04:35] Oscar: Sounds in the ballpark. Pricing? We need a sense of anchors so finance can sign.

[05:00] Liam: We'll send an updated pricing sheet. High level — committed monthly nodes at a discounted rate, burst usage billable at a lower overage rate than on-hosted. We can also provide a commitment Uplift credit if you sign for 12 months. I'll put the exact numbers in an email.

[05:40] Daniel: On the KMS side — do you support customer-managed keys in existing cloud KMS providers, and can we get a key rotation cadence?
[05:50] Maya: Yes, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for Private deployments. Rotation policies can be enforced through your KMS with automatic rewrap; we can document the rekey process during the security call.

[06:30] Oscar: For the pilot, we want to run a week of synthetic spikes that mirror our heaviest 24-hour windows and also a 48-hour soak. We want telemetry on tail latencies and token-level cost.
[06:45] Maya: That's doable. I'll stand up a test cluster in our APAC staging and run continuous batching profiles. We'll instrument token-level cost and latency traces.

[07:20] Priya: Also need to understand the KV cache warmup — first request experience is brutal for us right now. How does Redwood handle prefix caching across model versions?
[07:30] Maya: We persist KV cache per session for a given model version for the lifetime of the cache TTL. For rollout scenarios we replicate the prefix cache on warm-up instances; there is a short warmup penalty but the continuous batching helps amortize cost. We'll show you warming numbers in the runbook.

[08:15] Oscar: Who will be owning the SSO/roles? We need RBAC so non-devs can't spin up clusters.
[08:22] Liam: For Private and Dedicated we integrate with SAML/SCIM. We'll map roles to your AD groups and can gate provisioning. We'll draft a proposed RBAC mapping in the onboarding doc.

[09:05] Daniel: Audit retention — can you confirm log export formats and whether we can ship to our Splunk instance in real time?
[09:15] Maya: Yes, syslog/HTTPS export targets are supported; we can stream events and provide a JSON schema for the event types.

[09:45] Oscar: Ok good. On measurement and gating for signing: internal stakeholders expect latency p95 < 120ms for the inference-only calls in APAC, and cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll send the exact number). If those hit, finance will sign.
[10:05] Liam: We'll include those as measurable SLAs. For inference p95 at 120ms we recommend a mix of T4/RTX-class hardware in APAC; Maya will advise on right GPU profile during the perf run.

[11:00] Priya: Timeline: If we sign end of April, we want pilot running mid-May. Is that realistic?
[11:10] Maya: Yes — with the security deep-dive early April and your traffic profile we can spin the pilot by mid-May.

[11:45] Liam: Let's quick walk through the bench plan — Maya?
[11:48] Maya: Plan is: 1) run basic throughput baseline for current model family, 2) run 48-hour soak with synthetic spikes matching your histogram, 3) instrument tail latency and token-cost traces, 4) run failover scenarios with quantized variants to show graceful degradation. We'll provide notebooks and dashboards.

[12:25] Oscar: Can you also include a compare vs Apex Inference? They claim lower p95 in APAC but less observability.
[12:33] Liam: We'll include a short compare table focusing on observability and audit controls — but we'll avoid naming specifics in the doc except where you ask.

[13:10] Priya: For the contract, one more ask — can we have an auto-scale kicker to increase dedicated nodes if sustained qps exceeds threshold for N days instead of manual amendment?
[13:22] Liam: We can include policy-driven autoscaling with a notification hook for billing, and a threshold-based commit step if usage looks sustained beyond the grace period. We'll surface the exact mechanics in the SLA amendment.

[14:00] Daniel: Any constraints on private pilot regarding model variants or quantization? We need to be able to test the same model family we'll use in production (no forced downgrades).
[14:10] Maya: The private pilot can run the same family. For hardware constraints we may recommend a quantized variant for the burst pool to reduce token costs during spikes, but production steady-state can use the full-precision variant. We'll mark that in the runbook.

[15:00] Oscar: One small thing — during our internal load test last week we saw KV cache eviction that caused a correction in output quality. Can you log per-session cache hit rates?
[15:10] Maya: Yes, we can log per-session cache hit rates and provide a dashboard. We'll add KPI thresholds to the runbook.

[16:00] Liam: Alright, wrapping up — agreed items: 12-month renewal anchor, committed APAC capacity at ~1.5x sustained qps, shared burst bucket for seasonal spikes, 90-day private APAC pilot, security deep-dive, and the perf plan with a 48h soak.
[16:20] Oscar: Yep, that captures it.
[16:25] Priya: Thanks. We'll get the traffic profiles and stakeholders list to you by Friday.
[16:30] Liam: I'll follow up with the pricing and SLA amendment draft by Thursday, and Maya will kick off the perf cluster provisioning once we have the test account.
[16:45] Daniel: Ok — look forward to the security call — thanks everyone.
[16:50] Liam: Thanks team, talk soon.

End of transcript.
